subtype: Approach: working backward from months of cash left [Thinking]
passage: Gurpreet had savings for nine months. On the wall of the rented room in Pune he drew a line: last salary in March, savings run out in December. Then he counted backward. To raise money he would need proof by September, which meant a paying customer by August, which meant a working prototype by June. Gurleen, sitting cross-legged with the laptop, asked, "And the logo?" "Does the logo help us get a paying customer by August?" "No." "Then not now." Every task got the same test: does this help prove something by September? The list on the wall shrank from twenty-two items to seven. It felt frightening and calm at the same time.

qa.q: How many months of savings did Gurpreet have?
qa.a: Gurpreet had savings for nine months.

qa.q: What does "frightening and calm at the same time" suggest about how Gurpreet feels?
qa.a: It suggests Gurpreet feels fear of the deadline but also comfort from having a clear plan.

qa.q: What else could Gurpreet do to keep to the timeline?
qa.a: Gurpreet could check progress against the dates every week and speak to possible customers early.

qa.q: How might Gurleen see the logo question and the answer?
qa.a: Gurleen may see it as a fair test that cuts distractions, and accepts putting the logo aside.

grounding: Gurpreet counts back from the last salary date to work out what must be proven by month six and judges every task against that date.
